title: Reduce customer-facing error spikes by implementing per-tenant adaptive circuit-breakers and latency-aware retries
creator: Daniel Cho
description:
Summary:
During recent customer escalations (multiple high-revenue tenants) we've observed correlated 5xx spikes and long tail timeouts in the Hosted API. Those client retries amplified load and caused cascading connection pool exhaustion on frontends which in turn increased error rates for unaffected tenants. This ticket tracks the investigation, proposed fixes, canary rollout, and customer communications to mitigate immediate impact and prevent recurrence.

Observed symptoms:
- Multiple tenants reported increased 5xx and HTTP 504 timeouts between 2026-03-02 and 2026-03-04.
- Spike correlates with tenant bursts (large batch inference jobs) and coincides with higher connection resets on frontend pods.
- SDKs issued multiple retries within short windows; retry storms increased queueing on GPU workers.
- KV cache flushes on some model variants showed brief stalls which lengthened median latencies for affected routes.

Scope & impact:
- Affects Hosted API only; Dedicated and Private customers not observed to be affected yet.
- Immediate customer impact: high (some customers saw >30% of requests return 5xx for ~30m windows).
- Operational risk: potential for repeat incidents during peak tenant bursts.

Root cause hypothesis (current):
1) Global retry policy + aggressive per-SDK retry defaults allow clients to retry concurrently without tenant backoff awareness.
2) When a subset of tenants creates concentrated load, connection pool saturation occurs on edge proxies leading to server-side resets and timeouts.
3) KV cache flush locking introduces transient long-tail latencies for requests routed to nodes performing cache eviction/rehash.
4) Lack of a per-tenant degradation signal prevents graceful degradation (circuit breakers) and causes retries to exacerbate the hotspot.

Repro steps (internal):
- Use load generator to simulate tenant burst with 200 concurrent long generation requests (sequence length 1024) against model variant X.
- Configure client SDK to default retry=3, backoff=exponential. Observe connection pool metrics on frontends and request latencies on GPU workers.
- Trigger KV cache flush by rotating model quantization config to reproduce stall.

Proposed fixes (prioritized):
A) Short-term mitigations (hotfix, immediate):
  - Implement per-tenant sliding-window circuit breaker in frontends: trip on >20% 5xx or >3x baseline p95 latency in 1m window. When tripped, return a 429 with Retry-After and a structured header (X-Redwood-Tenant-Status) to indicate degraded mode.
  - Add server-side Retry-Control header to instruct SDKs to reduce retries (e.g., Retry-After values and max-retries override) during degraded windows.
  - Tune edge connection pool limits and idle timeouts to reduce resets under burst (frontend-side change, immediate canary).
B) Medium-term changes (this sprint):
  - Implement latency-aware client retry policy in SDKs (tenant-aware backoff + jitter + max-retries override from server headers).
  - Introduce a per-tenant backpressure token (leaky bucket) that gates request admission to downstream GPU workers.
  - Optimize KV cache flush to be incremental and non-blocking for in-flight KV lookups; reduce global locks and shard eviction.
C) Long-term (Q2+):
  - Workload-aware routing: route heavy tenants to isolated worker pools or dedicated capacity when thresholds are exceeded.
  - Expand rollout of model-variant fallback policies to automatically divert traffic to compatible smaller variants under pressure.

Canary / rollout plan:
- Stage 1 (hotfix): Deploy per-tenant circuit breaker and Retry-Control header to 10% of frontends (region-us-east-1) with feature flag enabled for 5 pilot customers. Monitor for false positives. Duration 48h.
- Stage 2: Expand to 50% frontends and enable SDK header consumption in internal SDK builds. Run load tests in staging against canary. Duration 72h.
- Stage 3: Full rollout across regions with gradual traffic ramp. Add automatic rollback if error rate increases beyond 2x baseline.

Monitoring & success metrics:
- Primary: reduction in 5xx rate for impacted tenants by >=80% within 30m of canary enablement.
- Secondary: decrease in average connection resubmits on frontends, p95 tail latency for generation requests, and customer reported incidents.
- Add new dashboards: tenant_error_rate (1m), tenant_latency_p95 (1m), frontend_conn_reset_rate (1m), retry-amplification-index (computed).
- Alerts: set PagerDuty alert if any tenant_error_rate > 5% for >10m after changes or if canary rollback triggered.

Testing & QA:
- Unit tests for circuit breaker and header semantics.
- Integration tests: simulated tenant burst + KV flush to validate early-fail and Retry-Control header behavior.
- Load test scale: reproduce at 2x typical daily peak in staging.

Customer communications (draft):
- Short-term: "We've implemented temporary protections to reduce elevated errors; you may see brief 429 responses indicating temporary throttling while we stabilize. Expected impact: lower tail errors and fewer retries. We're monitoring closely."
- Follow-up: postmortem with timeline and long-term mitigation plan within 7 business days.

Rollforward/rollback criteria:
- Roll forward: canary shows 80% reduction in 5xx for pilot tenants and no increase in latency >10% for unaffected tenants.
- Rollback: increase in global 5xx or latency or any severe degradation for non-pilot tenants or if the circuit breaker trips at >5% false-positive rate.

Security & compliance notes:
- Circuit breaker returns 429; no change to data plane or PII handling. No KMS/HSM changes. Security review not required for hotfix (code-level review still needed).

Follow-ups / open questions:
- Exact thresholds for per-tenant trip and cooldown window (suggested defaults in this ticket; need PM confirmation).
- SDK rollout cadence and backward-compat behavior for older SDKs that ignore Retry-Control.
- Whether to convert pilot tenants to Dedicated capacity automatically (needs product decision).

Artifacts & links:
- Runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood/hosted/retry-amplification-runbook (internal)
- Staging dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/hosted/tenant_errors
- Load test job: https://ci.redwood/jobs/loadtest/tenant-burst-2026-03
- RFC sketch: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1AdaptiveRetryRFC (internal)
comments: 2026-03-05 - Daniel Cho: Initial ticket created after post-incident triage. Collected preliminary metrics and set high priority. Assigned to Maya for implementation planning.

2026-03-06 - Maya Patel: Completed initial frontend prototype of per-tenant circuit breaker. Found that existing proxy layer had insufficient tenant tagging in logs; opened ENG-70215 to add tenant headers to proxy logs.

2026-03-07 - SRE Team (Liam O'Connor): Tuned connection pool on staging frontends and reduced reset rate by ~25% under synthetic load. Confirmed that connection reset amplification is a major contributor.
2026-03-09 - Maya Patel: Hotfix branch created: github.com/redwood-inference/hosted-proxy/pull/982 (circuit-breaker + Retry-Control header). Running unit tests and internal integration tests.

2026-03-11 - QA (Rina Gupta): Integration load tests in staging reproducing retry amplification. Verified that circuit breaker triggers for simulated tenant bursts; observed 70% reduction in 5xx during tests.
2026-03-12 - Maya Patel: Started canary in us-east-1 for 2 pilot tenants. Early telemetry looks promising; one tenant observed brief 429s but overall reduced errors. Monitoring for false positives.
2026-03-14 - Daniel Cho: Pulled in SDK team to coordinate Retry-Control header handling and client-side backoff changes. Planning medium-term SDK release in Cycle 2026-W12.
